title: A kernel-checked bound Lambda <= 9/32 for the de Bruijn-Newman constant from OpenAI's quasi-Riemann hypothesis
description: Lean 4 formalization, verification scripts, audit records and paper for the bound Lambda <= 9/32 on the de Bruijn-Newman constant, obtained by composing OpenAI's kernel-checked quasi-Riemann hypothesis (riemannZeta s != 0 for Re s > 7/8; openai/math, commit adc7f124, Apache-2.0) with de Bruijn's 1950 heat-flow theorem as formalized on the Arda dbn island, in one Lean environment at OpenAI's Mathlib pin. The theorem (every zero of H_t is real for every t >= 9/32) depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; it was re-checked by a second kernel (nanoda) through openai/ten-proofs Comparator against a challenge that imports only Mathlib, with a tampered challenge rejected; independently audited; and judged in CI against the registered statement. It is the first bound below de Bruijn's 1/2 that is kernel-checked end to end. It is weaker than the numerical bounds 0.22 (Polymath15) and 0.2 (Platt-Trudgian), and it is not the Riemann Hypothesis. Not yet refereed. Licensing: Lean sources and scripts Apache-2.0; paper and prose CC-BY-4.0; OpenAI's theorem is theirs under Apache-2.0 and is not vendored.
